title: Running with Obstacles
statementMd:
A sportsman starts from point $*x*_{*start*} = 0$ and runs to point with coordinate $*x*_{*finish*} = *m*$ (on a straight line). Also, the sportsman can jump — to jump, he should first take a run of length of not less than $*s*$ meters (in this case for these $*s*$ meters his path should have no obstacles), and after that he can jump over a length of not more than $*d*$ meters. Running and jumping is permitted only in the direction from left to right. He can **start** and**finish** a jump only at the points with integer coordinates in which there are **no obstacles**. To overcome some obstacle, it is necessary to land at a point which is strictly to the right of this obstacle.

On the way of an athlete are $*n*$ obstacles at coordinates $*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$. He cannot go over the obstacles, he can only jump over them. Your task is to determine whether the athlete will be able to get to the finish point.

## Input

The first line of the input containsd four integers $*n*$, $*m*$, $*s*$ and $*d*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$, $2 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9}$, $1 ≤ *s*, *d* ≤ 10^{9}$) — the number of obstacles on the runner's way, the coordinate of the finishing point, the length of running before the jump and the maximum length of the jump, correspondingly.

The second line contains a sequence of $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ *m* - 1$) — the coordinates of the obstacles. It is guaranteed that the starting and finishing point have no obstacles, also no point can have more than one obstacle, The coordinates of the obstacles are given in an arbitrary order.

## Output

If the runner cannot reach the finishing point, print in the first line of the output "`IMPOSSIBLE`" (without the quotes).

If the athlete can get from start to finish, print any way to do this in the following format:

- print a line of form "`RUN X`>" (where "`X`" should be a positive integer), if the athlete should run for "`X`" more meters;
- print a line of form "`JUMP Y`" (where "`Y`" should be a positive integer), if the sportsman starts a jump and should remain in air for "`Y`" more meters.

All commands "`RUN`" and "`JUMP`" should strictly alternate, starting with "`RUN`", besides, they should be printed chronologically. It is not allowed to jump over the finishing point but it is allowed to land there after a jump. The athlete should stop as soon as he reaches finish.
statementZhMd:
运动员从坐标为 $*x*_{*start*} = 0$ 的点出发，沿直线跑向坐标为 $*x*_{*finish*} = *m*$ 的点。此外，运动员还可以跳跃——要进行跳跃，他必须先助跑不少于 $*s*$ 米（在这 $*s*$ 米的路程中不能有障碍物），之后他可以跳过不超过 $*d*$ 米的距离。跑步和跳跃都只能沿从左到右的方向进行。他只能在坐标为整数且**没有障碍物**的点开始和结束跳跃。为了越过某个障碍物，必须落在严格位于该障碍物右侧的点上。

运动员的路线上有 $*n*$ 个障碍物，坐标分别为 $*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$。他不能跑过障碍物，只能跳过它们。请判断运动员是否能够到达终点。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含四个整数 $*n*, $*m*$, $*s*$ 和 $*d*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$, $2 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9}$, $1 ≤ *s*, *d* ≤ 10^{9}$）——运动员路上的障碍物数量、终点坐标、跳跃前的助跑距离以及跳跃的最大距离。

第二行包含一个由 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ 组成的序列（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ *m* - 1$）——障碍物的坐标。保证起点和终点没有障碍物，且每个点至多有一个障碍物。障碍物坐标以任意顺序给出。

## 输出格式

如果运动员无法到达终点，在输出的第一行打印 “`IMPOSSIBLE`”（不含引号）。

如果运动员能够从起点到达终点，请按照以下格式输出任意一种可行方案：

- 如果运动员应再跑 $X$ 米，输出一行 “`RUN X`>”（其中 “$X$” 应为正整数）；
- 如果运动员开始跳跃，并应在空中再移动 $Y$ 米，输出一行 “`JUMP Y`”（其中 “$Y$” 应为正整数）。

所有的 “`RUN`” 和 “`JUMP`” 指令必须严格交替出现，并且从 “`RUN`” 开始；此外，它们应按时间顺序输出。不允许跳过终点，但允许在跳跃后落在终点。运动员到达终点后应立即停止。
